database-fundamentals-001.title: Purpose of a DBMS
database-fundamentals-001.instructions: Select the one correct answer. What is the primary purpose of a Database Management System (DBMS)?
options: To create application interfaces.
To manage, maintain, query and secure databases.
To replace the data stored by an organization.
To define the organization's business strategy.
database-fundamentals-001.explanation: A DBMS is the software layer used to manage, maintain, query and secure a database.

database-fundamentals-002.title: Benefits of the Database Approach
database-fundamentals-002.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which are benefits of the database approach described in the course?
options: Multiple users and applications can access shared data, with concurrency control.
Unnecessary data duplication can be reduced.
Centralized security controls can manage who accesses or modifies data.
The physical order of rows determines the meaning of a relational table.
database-fundamentals-002.explanation: The database approach supports shared data, reduces unnecessary redundancy and provides centralized security monitoring. Relational table rows have no inherent order.

relational-tables-001.title: Properties of Relational Tables
relational-tables-001.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements describe properties of relational tables?
options: Each cell contains one single attribute value.
Every row in a table is unique.
Rows have no inherent order.
The order of columns carries inherent meaning.
relational-tables-001.explanation: Relational tables have atomic attribute values, unique rows and unordered rows. Column names are unique, but column order carries no inherent meaning.

database-fundamentals-003.title: Database, DBMS and RDBMS
database-fundamentals-003.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements correctly describe these terms?
options: A database is an integrated collection of data and metadata.
A DBMS is the software layer used to manage a database.
An RDBMS is based on the relational model.
A database contains metadata only and does not contain data.
database-fundamentals-003.explanation: The course defines a database as an integrated collection containing data and metadata, a DBMS as the management software, and an RDBMS as a DBMS based on the relational model.

keys-and-relationships-001.title: Purpose of a Primary Key
keys-and-relationships-001.instructions: Select the one correct answer. What is the main purpose of a primary key?
options: To uniquely identify each row in a table.
To store several values in one cell.
To determine the order of rows.
To store the description of every column.
keys-and-relationships-001.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies rows in a table. It must contain a valid, non-NULL value.

keys-and-relationships-002.title: Choosing a Primary Key
keys-and-relationships-002.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements about choosing a primary key are supported by the course material?
options: A primary key uniquely identifies rows.
A meaningless surrogate key is recommended over a meaningful key.
Meaningful data may change over time, which can complicate references.
A primary key is allowed to contain NULL values.
keys-and-relationships-002.explanation: The course recommends a meaningless surrogate key because meaningful values may change over time and complicate references. A primary key must always contain a valid, non-NULL value.

keys-and-relationships-003.title: Foreign Key Rules
keys-and-relationships-003.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements about foreign keys are correct according to the course?
options: A foreign key references the primary key of another table.
The data types of the foreign key and referenced primary key must match exactly.
The foreign-key population must be a subset of the referenced primary-key population.
A foreign key must always contain unique values.
keys-and-relationships-003.explanation: A foreign key establishes a relationship by referencing another table's primary key. The data types must match, and referential integrity requires its population to be a subset of the referenced primary-key population.

multiplicities-001.title: Relationship Multiplicities
multiplicities-001.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which multiplicity definitions are correct?
options: 1 means exactly one.
0..1 means zero or one.
0..* means zero or many.
1..* means zero or many.
multiplicities-001.explanation: The course defines 1 as exactly one, 0..1 as zero or one, 0..* as zero or many, and 1..* as one or many.

data-modeling-001.title: Modeling Lifecycle Order
data-modeling-001.instructions: Select the one correct answer. Which sequence follows the modeling chain presented in the course?
options: Physical Data Model → Domain Model → Logical Data Model → Design Model
Wireframes and interviews → Domain Model → Behavior Modeling → Design Model → Logical Data Model → Physical Data Model
Domain Model → Physical Data Model → Wireframes and interviews → Logical Data Model
Behavior Modeling → Physical Data Model → Domain Model → Wireframes and interviews
data-modeling-001.explanation: The course presents the lifecycle as wireframes/interviews, Domain Model, behavior modeling, Design Model, Logical Data Model and finally Physical Data Model.

data-modeling-002.title: Logical and Physical Models
data-modeling-002.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements distinguish the Logical Data Model from the Physical Data Model?
options: The Logical Data Model establishes primary keys, foreign keys and constraints such as unique and not-null.
The Physical Data Model adds specific data types for the chosen DBMS.
The Physical Data Model can include database objects and indexes.
The Domain Model contains foreign keys and database-specific indexes.
data-modeling-002.explanation: The Logical Data Model defines keys, constraints and naming standards. The Physical Data Model adds DBMS-specific data types, objects, indexes and technical constraints. The Domain Model contains business concepts without foreign keys.

database-roles-001.title: Responsibilities in a Database Environment
database-roles-001.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which responsibilities are correctly matched to the database roles?
options: The Data Administrator is responsible for data governance.
The Database Administrator is responsible for technical implementation and maintenance.
The Application Developer builds applications that interface with the database.
The End User is technically responsible for maintaining database performance.
database-roles-001.explanation: The Data Administrator handles data governance, the DBA handles technical implementation, performance and maintenance, and the Application Developer builds applications that use the database. End Users use the database indirectly through application interfaces.

relational-integrity-001.title: Domain, Population and NULL
relational-integrity-001.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements correctly describe relational database terminology?
options: A domain is the collection of all possible valid values for an attribute.
A population is the set of concrete values currently present in an attribute or table.
NULL represents a missing or unknown value.
A domain is always identical to the values currently stored in the table.
relational-integrity-001.explanation: A domain describes all values permitted for an attribute, while a population describes the concrete values currently present. NULL denotes a missing or unknown value.

sql-language-001.title: Declarative SQL
sql-language-001.instructions: Select the one correct answer. What does it mean that SQL is a declarative language?
options: The user specifies the desired result rather than every procedural step.
The user must describe every internal database operation.
SQL can only be used inside an application programming language.
SQL automatically defines the organization's data standards.
sql-language-001.explanation: SQL is declarative because users state what they want to achieve, rather than specifying the exact procedural steps for achieving it.

sql-language-002.title: SQL Subcategories
sql-language-002.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which SQL commands are correctly assigned to their subcategories in the course?
options: SELECT belongs to DQL.
INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE belong to DML.
CREATE, ALTER and DROP belong to DDL.
GRANT and REVOKE belong to transaction control.
sql-language-002.explanation: The course classifies SELECT as DQL, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE as DML, CREATE/ALTER/DROP as DDL, and GRANT/REVOKE as DCL. COMMIT, ROLLBACK and SAVEPOINT are transaction-control commands.

sql-language-003.title: SQL Execution Modes
sql-language-003.instructions: Select all correct answers. According to the course, how can SQL be used?
options: Interactively, through direct queries.
Embedded within host programming languages.
Embedded in languages such as Java, C and C#.
Only through a spreadsheet application.
sql-language-003.explanation: The course describes interactive use through direct queries and embedded use within host programming languages, including Java, C and C#.

sql-language-004.title: SELECT Without FROM
sql-language-004.instructions: Select the one correct answer. What can PostgreSQL do with SELECT when no FROM clause is present?
options: It can evaluate scalar expressions, calculations or system variables.
It must return an error because FROM is mandatory.
It automatically selects every table in the database.
It can only return metadata about columns.
sql-language-004.explanation: The course notes that SELECT can evaluate scalar expressions, calculations and system variables without querying a table.

sql-execution-order-001.title: Logical SQL Execution Order
sql-execution-order-001.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements about the logical execution order are correct?
options: FROM is evaluated before WHERE.
WHERE is evaluated before GROUP BY.
HAVING is evaluated after GROUP BY.
ORDER BY is evaluated before DISTINCT.
sql-execution-order-001.explanation: The relevant order is FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT and ORDER BY. Therefore the first three statements are correct, while DISTINCT precedes ORDER BY.

text-comparisons-001.title: Case Sensitivity in Text Comparisons
text-comparisons-001.instructions: Select the one correct answer. According to the course material, how are literal text comparisons evaluated?
options: They are always case-insensitive.
They are strictly case-sensitive.
They automatically convert both values to uppercase.
They ignore capitalization only when values contain spaces.
text-comparisons-001.explanation: The course states that literal text comparisons are strictly case-sensitive. UPPER() and LOWER() can be used to standardize text for uniform comparison.

type-conversion-001.title: Implicit and Explicit Conversion
type-conversion-001.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements about type conversion are correct?
options: Implicit conversions are performed automatically by the database engine.
Implicit conversions can depend on client or system configuration.
Explicit conversions can use functions such as CAST, TO_CHAR and TO_DATE.
Explicit conversions rely on the active system defaults instead of specifying the conversion.
type-conversion-001.explanation: Implicit conversions happen automatically and can depend on configuration. Explicit conversions use functions such as TO_CHAR, TO_DATE, TO_NUMBER or CAST to make type compatibility more predictable.

date-formatting-001.title: PostgreSQL DateStyle
date-formatting-001.instructions: Select the one correct answer. What does the DateStyle setting influence in PostgreSQL?
options: How date inputs are interpreted and outputs are formatted.
How primary keys are selected.
How rows are grouped by aggregate functions.
How foreign-key data types are matched.
date-formatting-001.explanation: PostgreSQL interprets date inputs and formats date outputs according to the active DateStyle parameter. The course recommends using explicit formatting masks rather than relying on system defaults.

numeric-formatting-001.title: Numeric Formatting Modifiers
numeric-formatting-001.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements about numeric TO_CHAR format modifiers are correct?
options: 9 represents a digit position that is dropped if insignificant.
0 retains a digit position, including leading zeros when insignificant.
FM suppresses leading zeros and blank padding spaces.
L represents the localized decimal separator.
numeric-formatting-001.explanation: The course defines 9 as an optional digit position, 0 as a retained digit position, and FM as Fill Mode, which suppresses leading zeros and blank padding. L represents the localized currency symbol; D and G represent localized decimal and group separators.

numeric-functions-001.title: ROUND and TRUNC
numeric-functions-001.instructions: Select the one correct answer. What is the main difference between ROUND() and TRUNC()?
options: ROUND removes digits without rounding, while TRUNC rounds them.
ROUND rounds to a specified precision, while TRUNC removes digits without rounding.
Both functions always return the same result.
TRUNC only works with negative numbers.
numeric-functions-001.explanation: ROUND() rounds a number to the specified precision. TRUNC() truncates toward zero without rounding.

numeric-functions-002.title: Numeric Function Rules
numeric-functions-002.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements about ROUND() and TRUNC() are correct?
options: ROUND() breaks ties by rounding away from zero.
A negative precision in ROUND() rounds positions to the left of the decimal point.
TRUNC() truncates toward zero without rounding.
TRUNC(15256, -1) returns 15260.
numeric-functions-002.explanation: ROUND() rounds ties away from zero, and negative precision rounds tens, hundreds and other positions to the left of the decimal point. TRUNC() removes digits toward zero without rounding; the course example gives TRUNC(15256, -1) = 15250.

numeric-functions-003.title: Purpose of MOD
numeric-functions-003.instructions: Select the one correct answer. What does MOD(y, x) return?
options: The remainder of y divided by x.
The average of y and x.
The rounded value of y multiplied by x.
The difference between y and x.
numeric-functions-003.explanation: MOD(y, x) returns the remainder of y/x. If y is a multiple of x, the result is zero; if x is greater than y, the result is y.

joins-001.title: Cartesian Product
joins-001.instructions: Select the one correct answer. Table A contains 4 rows and Table B contains 3 rows. If both tables are included in the FROM clause without a join condition, how many row combinations are produced?
options: 7 combinations.
4 combinations.
12 combinations.
3 combinations.
joins-001.explanation: A Cartesian product pairs every row in the first table with every row in the second table. The total is 4 × 3 = 12 combinations.

joins-002.title: Ambiguous Column References
joins-002.instructions: Select all correct answers. Two joined tables both contain a column named department_id. Which statements are correct?
options: Referencing department_id without a qualifier can produce an ambiguity error.
A table alias or qualifier can identify which column is intended.
The ambiguity occurs because both tables contain a column with the same name.
The database always chooses the first table's column automatically.
joins-002.explanation: When joined tables share a column name, an unqualified reference can be ambiguous. Qualifying the column with its table name or alias resolves the ambiguity.

joins-003.title: NATURAL JOIN and USING
joins-003.instructions: Select all correct answers. Which statements about NATURAL JOIN and USING match the course material?
options: NATURAL JOIN automatically equates columns with identical names across the tables.
NATURAL JOIN can produce unintended results when tables share unexpected column names.
USING explicitly specifies the common column used for the join.
Table aliases can be used on the joined column specified in USING.
joins-003.explanation: NATURAL JOIN uses all identically named columns, which can introduce unintended join conditions. USING explicitly names the common join column, but table aliases are not permitted on that joined column. The course also notes that aliases cannot be used with NATURAL JOIN.

aggregate-functions-001.title: Nested Aggregate Functions
aggregate-functions-001.instructions: Select the one correct answer. Why does PostgreSQL reject directly nesting aggregate functions such as AVG(MAX(salary))?
options: Aggregate functions cannot operate on numeric values.
Direct nesting of aggregate function calls is logically invalid.
AVG() can only be used with text values.
MAX() always requires a join condition.
aggregate-functions-001.explanation: Aggregate functions operate on groups of rows to return a single result per group. Directly nesting aggregate function calls is logically invalid and PostgreSQL raises an error.
